title: Höpken-Carlson volume, Constantinople, 1742 (catalogue 2244): the Khan of Crimea's letter to the King of Sweden in the second Höpken code, read from its contemporary gloss and checked group by group against the frozen hopken1740 key, with a held-out test of that key

documents.shelfmark: Stockholm, Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, SE/RA/2119/2119.1/I/9/28 (image series R0003637), images 227, 228 (two pages) and 229
documents.date: enclosure to Carlson's despatch of 10/21 May 1742 (endorsement); the extract ends 'au commencement du mois de mai 1742'
documents.route: the Khan of Crimea -> the King of Sweden (French translation, as headed); enclosure to Carlson's despatch to the chancery president (endorsement)

plaintext.source: Contemporary French decipherment written over the struck cipher groups; one row (B07, 12 groups) and a few stretches where the glossing hand drew only a line have none.

transcription.source: Riksarkivet IIIF images, full size (lbiiif.riksarkivet.se), R0003637
transcription.notes: Two passes by one agent (bands at 0.72-0.8x, half-width crops at 1.4-1.5x), digits only; the gloss was in view but read separately, after the digits. A third pass after the first decryption re-read 23 groups on images 227 and 229 as 8 (this hand's looped 8 looks like a 2); the key-blind file is kept. 14 cipher words contain a doubtful digit. 614 groups (161 distinct, strokes and ? marks set aside) in 60 rows; the clear date 1742 is not counted.

system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups, here between 1006 and 1913, a syllabary built for Swedish with word codes (1516 ottporten = Porte, 1360 tractat = traité, 1450 alliance, 1265 swerige = Suède, 1430 minister; here also 1903 Perse and 1913 Chan, from the gloss). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d').
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the entries of key.tsv (373 entries, 374 lines with the header): the 352 entries of key_frozen.tsv (= targets/hopken1740/key_1741.tsv) plus 21 values from this gloss. This document has 161 distinct groups, 135 of them in the frozen key.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary French decipherment written over the groups on images 227-229. No edition or modern decipherment found (web search, 12 Nov 2026). The Khan's original letter may survive among Riksarkivet's Turcica; not checked.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, applied the frozen key, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (fetch, crop, decryption, held-out test, mark check)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: Images 226-229 of R0003637 fetched from the Riksarkivet IIIF service at full size.
Two passes, digits only, then the gloss read into gloss_khan1742.tsv before any decryption; disagreements settled on 1.4-1.5x crops and 3x zooms (transcription_khan1742_blind.txt).
The frozen hopken1740 key (key_frozen.tsv, byte for byte targets/hopken1740/key_1741.tsv, 352 entries) applied unchanged; frozen before any group of these pages was decrypted (FROZEN.sha256).

Held-out test (scripts/heldout.py) of the frozen key against the contemporary gloss on the key-blind transcription: 487 of the 602 glossed groups give exactly the gloss letters at their place (81%; 88% of the 554 in the key); with the key's values shuffled, mean 63.2 and maximum 103 over 300 shuffles. Images 227 and 229 alone: 214 of 282 (shuffled maximum 50).

Pass 3 after the first decryption: 23 groups on images 227 and 229 re-read as 8 (22 of them 2 -> 8, one 7 -> 8) on 1.6x row crops; the rule was added to SIGN_CONVENTIONS.md before image 228 was transcribed. 22 of the 256 cipher words rest on these re-reads.

Mechanical decryption, marked reading (scripts/check_marks.py passes, and fails on a tampered file), French reading and English translation. 256 cipher words: 205 verbatim from the frozen key, 23 repaired, 28 from the gloss only, 0 holes. docs/_check_reading.py: clean share 0.900 (27 of 30 sentences).
key.tsv = the frozen key plus 21 values read from this gloss (status gloss_1742) and one correction (1324 pp -> et, at four places).

Image 482 (Carlson's despatch of 22 Sept 1742, three Swedish-glossed blocks and a Lit. A) looked at: groups run to 2959 and 'Castellane' is 1531 1733 1442 1034 1182, which the hopken1740 key does not give; a different code, not worked.

One web search (the Khan of Crimea's letter to the King of Sweden, 1742, Porte, secours, défensive): no edition or decipherment of this extract. A 2002 study of Crimean Tatar letters to Sweden (Pis'mennye pamyatniki Vostoka 8) was found and not opened; the Khan's original letter may survive among Riksarkivet's Turcica, not checked.

Blind review by an independent AI language-model agent that took no part in the solve: 96 groups in 8 rows (A05, A06, A09, A13 on image 227; C13, D11 on 228; B06, B12 on 229) copied from its own crops before it opened the transcription, with no disagreement beyond the documented 8/2 shape; FROZEN.sha256, decrypt.py, check_marks.py and heldout.py reproduced (100 shuffles: mean 62.8, maximum 103); the reading read as French sentences against the translation, grade A.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py) of the mechanical text with the frozen key (scripts/validation_pairs_1742.py; the 30 groups not in the frozen key left out): 584 tokens, 135 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.075 per letter; random keys -3.633 (z 13.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.453 (mean -2.467, z 47.8); annealer on the real text -2.388. Verdict: pass. The key was not fitted to these pages.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.075; polyphony 0.0; 30 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.388

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The frozen hopken1740 key (key_1741.tsv) read the cipher and was tested held-out against the contemporary French gloss (487 of 602 groups); 21 values were added from the gloss.
outcome.fraction_read_source: scripts/check_marks.py with key_frozen.tsv: 205 of 256 cipher words verbatim from the signs (80.1%; 228 of 256, 89.1%, with marked repairs). fraction_coherent counts the words that read as sense with the contemporary gloss: 256 of 256 (the 28 words over groups the frozen key lacks rest on the gloss; 0 holes). Clear words between the groups are not counted. Counted on the key alone the extent would be read in part.

texts.label: Lit. A: extract of the translation of the Khan of Crimea's letter to the King of Sweden, May 1742
texts.summary: The Khan, after reaching the Porte, tells the King of Sweden that the delay in executing the Swedish-Ottoman defensive alliance comes only from the Porte's need to fortify its frontier with Persia; aid promised to friends is conditional, so aid to Sweden is difficult, but the Ottoman Empire values Sweden's friendship and will give all the aid it can in the present circumstances.
texts.note: 256 cipher words: 205 verbatim from the frozen key (80.1%), 23 repaired, 28 from the gloss only, 0 holes; 22 of the verbatim words rest on a pass-3 digit re-read. Held-out: 487 of the 602 glossed groups match the gloss (81%; 88% of the 554 in the key; shuffled maximum 103 over 300 shuffles). Checker clean share 0.900 (reading, 27 of 30 sentences), 0.912 (translation). A contemporary decipherment checked against the key; the bare runs of the volume remain open.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: the whole extract reads, with no holes; 205 of 256 cipher words come verbatim from the frozen hopken1740 key, 23 with marked repairs and 28 from the contemporary gloss over groups the key lacks. 96 groups in 8 rows on all three images were spot-checked on the scans with no disagreement beyond the documented 8/2 shape.

outcome.notes: One document over three images (227, 228 with two pages, 229). It applies targets/hopken1740/key_1741.tsv byte for byte, so it could be folded into targets/hopken1740 (one key, one entry), as was done with hopken1741a and hopken1741b. It is a contemporary decipherment checked against the key. Not part of this target and not worked: the bare runs of the volume (images 198, 246, 342 and others), the other glossed passages (29, 86, 114, 397, 539) and image 482 in another code; the catalogue entry treats the glossed passages as cribs, so catalogue 2244 is not closed (see NOTES).
